meta.title: Who really said "Give me an army of West Point graduates, I'll win a battle. Give me a handful of Texas Aggies and I'll win a war!"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: No record shows Patton said it. The Aggie line first surfaces in a 1993 Usenet post, and the Patton Society calls it an urban legend.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Give me an army of West Point graduates, I'll win a battle. Give me a handful of Texas Aggies and I'll win a war!'?
meta.ogDescription: Pinned on Patton, a West Point man, with no source. The earliest citation found is a 1993 Usenet post. Other schools claim the same line.

answer.label: Not George S. Patton — unsourced campus lore
answer.authorDates: Origin unknown · earliest citation found: Usenet, 1993
answer.sourceLine: No documented Patton source contains this line. Wikiquote lists it as misattributed, and The Patton Society’s founder calls it an urban legend. The earliest citation Barry Popik found is a 30 September 1993 post to the Usenet group alt.quotations.

source.excerpt: Give me an army of West Point graduates, I’ll win a battle. Give me a handful of Texas Aggies and I’ll win a war!
trail: Wikiquote ↗ lists the line in its “Misattributed” section of Patton quotations.
Barry Popik’s entry ↗ (1 August 2007) says no source has been found. His earliest citation is a 30 September 1993 alt.quotations post by Raoul Rodriguez.

In the Texas A&M Battalion (2 October 2006), as quoted on Wikiquote ↗, Patton Society founder Mike Province said: “I honestly don’t believe he said it, because I’ve heard too many people say that he said it about their school.”
The attribution went on anyway. Rep. Ted Poe read it into the Congressional Record ↗ on 30 November 2018 as something “General George S. Patton once said.”
source.excerptNote: This is the popular wording, as Wikiquote records it under “Misattributed.” Barry Popik transcribes the 1993 Usenet version as “Give me an Army of West Point Graduates, and I’ll win a battle. Give me a handful of Texas Aggies and I’ll win a war.” That post credits it to “Patton (who graduated from West Point).” Popik also records the shorter “Give me a handful of Texas Aggies, and I’ll win a war!”

author.name: Anonymous (Texas A&M lore)
author.heading: Who actually originated it
author.metaLine: Unknown originator · line first seen in a 1993 Usenet post
author.bio: Nobody knows who wrote the line. It circulates as Texas A&M Corps of Cadets lore and turns up on Aggie T-shirts and websites, but no one has traced it to a named author. The man it is pinned on, George S. Patton (1885–1945), graduated from West Point in 1909, which makes him an odd choice to belittle West Point graduates.

misattribution.heading: Why it gets pinned on Patton
misattribution.intro: This is a school-pride line. Credited to a famous general, it carries more weight than an unsigned slogan would. The same line, with the school swapped, gets credited to Patton for several institutions.

items.why: No speech, letter or book of his contains it, and Wikiquote lists it as misattributed ↗. He was a West Point graduate himself (class of 1909 ↗).
Patton Society founder Mike Province told the Battalion in 2006 that “People will use it with Texas Aggies, The Citadel, Virginia Military Institute and even Clemson” (quoted on Wikiquote ↗).
His tribute “The Fightin’ Texas Aggie Corps of Cadets: 142 Years of Tradition” credits the line to Patton with no source (govinfo ↗).

misattribution.truthLine: Nobody has found a source tying the line to Patton. The earliest citation Barry Popik found is a 1993 Usenet post (Popik ↗), and the line’s true originator is unknown.

context.heading: Why the story sticks
lead: The quote flatters Texas A&M’s Corps of Cadets by having a famous West Point general put a handful of Aggies above a whole army of his own academy’s graduates. That twist makes it memorable, and it is also a reason to doubt it. Patton graduated from West Point in 1909 ↗, after a year at the Virginia Military Institute.

When the line was asked about on the Straight Dope message board in 2006, no one in the thread ↗ produced a primary source. The original poster said he had found it only on Corps of Cadets and Aggie alumni websites.
context.detailsSummary: If any school could claim Patton
detailsBody: Wikiquote’s editors note ↗ that if any school has a claim, it is VMI. Patton’s father, grandfather and grand-uncles graduated from VMI, and he spent a year there before going to West Point. This does not make the quote genuine for VMI either. No version of the line has a documented Patton source.
context.pull: I’ve heard too many people say that he said it about their school.
